- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day forecast.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing near-term price momentum.
- After sharp price spikes in history, model overreacts with excessive overshoot in the immediate forecast window.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the latter half of the forecast — often overestimates prices when history shows downward drift.
- Forecasts for the last 5–7 days are often too high, especially when true outcomes show a downward trend or stabilization.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward lower values, particularly when historical prices are above 65–70 — underestimates by 5–10% on average.
- Forecasts for the first 10 days are systematically too low, while the last 10 days are often too high — suggesting asymmetric error structure.
- Model does not adjust for seasonality or policy-driven volatility (e.g., auction dates, compliance deadlines) — leading to persistent bias in mid-to-late forecast horizon.
